description: A symbolic pattern database is a planning heuristic computed with BDDs (*binary decision diagrams*). A *pattern* is a subset of the task variables, and the task is projected onto it: all other variables are removed, which gives a much smaller task. A blind backward Dijkstra in this projection runs to the end and stores the goal distances as one BDD per value `h`. A state gets the distance of its projection, and a state whose projection cannot reach the goal is a dead end. The heuristic is *admissible* (it never overestimates) and *consistent* (it drops by at most the cost of each operator), so it suits BDDA* and other optimal searches.

papers.title: Symbolic Pattern Databases in Heuristic Search Planning
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Planning Systems (AIPS)
